basis: Immune-mediated intermediate uveitis affecting the pars plana; associated systemic autoimmune diseases are separate conditions.
Hereditary degeneration of the choroid; broad neurodegenerative ancestry does not establish extraocular neurologic disease.
Immune-mediated inflammation of cutaneous vessel walls defines both skin and vascular involvement; systemic organ damage is not required.
Defined skeletal myopathy with defective protein O-glycosylation; brain and eye involvement cannot be assumed across the full myopathy spectrum.
Developmental brain dysfunction and seizures dominate; nystagmus/strabismus alone do not establish eye damage; optic atrophy 1/8, cerebral visual impairment 2/8.
Inherited metabolic disorder defined by hyperammonemic encephalopathy; liver injury is not established by hyperammonemia alone.
Glycosylation disorder with eye and limb malformations; developmental impairment 80-99%; cap excludes frequent cleft palate, pulmonic stenosis and microtia.
Short-rib thoracic dysplasia causes characteristic respiratory insufficiency and pulmonary hypoplasia in most; renal and retinal findings are occasional, 5-29%.
This concept denotes the cataract complication itself; the underlying myotonic dystrophy is a separate disease.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the CNS; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis, and the disease is associated with HIV.
Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias defined by stippled bone calcification; additional organ and metabolic findings vary by subtype.
Broad thoracic umbrella has no uniform organ axis; pulmonary is an approximate assignment. Breast, cardiac, mediastinal and chest-wall subtypes differ.
Bone dysplasia and bone sarcoma syndrome classified under polyamine metabolism disorders; cataract frequency is unspecified, so ocular involvement is omitted.
Focal or multifocal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; laryngeal and limb dystonia do not establish intrinsic airway or muscle damage.
Chronic bronchial inflammation, mucus hypersecretion and airflow obstruction; ordinary smoking-related inflammation does not imply an immune-mediated disease.
Skeletal dysplasia with progressive degenerative joint disease; the definition explicitly excludes ophthalmologic and cleft-palate abnormalities.
Carcinoma confined to the uterine cervical epithelium; reproductive organs have no axis, and no infection is specified by this concept.
Classified as bacterial infection of the fetal membranes; the obstetric site has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Inherited coagulation abnormality causing activated protein C resistance; venous thrombosis is a separate disease whose risk is increased.
Osteochondrodysplasia with malformed digits, scoliosis and joint dysfunction; absent skin creases reflect digit malformation rather than skin damage.
Benign neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells; skin, bone and breast locations are variable subtypes rather than universal additional organ involvement.
Nephrocerebral syndrome with developmental impairment, brain atrophy and glomerular disease; optic atrophy occurs in 13/14 patients.
Congenital unilateral fusion of the humerus, radius and ulna; no additional organ disease is established.
Inherited renal tubular urate transport defect causes urinary urate wasting and hypouricemia; stones and kidney injury remain within the renal axis.
Infantile epilepsy with progressive encephalopathy and cortical atrophy; hypotonia and ataxia are manifestations of the neurologic disease.
